subproblem.title: Count nonunits modulo a prime power
subproblem.statement: For natural numbers p and a with p prime and 0 < a, the subtype of nonunits in ℤ/p^aℤ has natural cardinality p^(a−1): Nat.card {z : ZMod (p^a) // ¬ IsUnit z} = p^(a−1).
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (p a : ℕ), p.Prime → 0 < a → Nat.card {z : ZMod (p ^ a) // ¬ IsUnit z} = p ^ (a - 1)
subproblem.natural_proof: 1. Fix a prime p and a positive integer a, and put q=p^a and b=p^(a−1). Since p≥2 and a=(a−1)+1, we have p>0, b>0, and q=p b>0. Each z∈Z/qZ has a unique natural representative z.val with 0≤z.val0 imply k
proof_key_steps: Write p^a = p · p^(a−1), with both factors positive.
Identify nonunits with residues whose canonical representatives are divisible by p.
Send k < p^(a−1) to the residue of pk, whose representative is exactly pk.
Prove injectivity by equality of canonical representatives and cancellation of p.
Prove surjectivity by dividing the representative of a nonunit by p.
Transfer Nat.card along the bijection with Fin (p^(a−1)).

audit.reason: The single-line proposition exactly matches the nonunit subtype, hypotheses and natural cardinality in the prose. It elaborates independently with the ordinary ZMod unit predicate; its bare identifier is unreserved. Step 1 establishes positive modulus and p^a = p·p^(a−1). Step 2 correctly characterizes nonunits through divisibility of canonical representatives. Steps 3–5 construct the map from Fin (p^(a−1)), establish its range, prove injectivity by bounded representatives and cancellation, and prove surjectivity by divisibility and the representative bound. Step 6 transfers cardinality correctly, including a=1. No classification lemma or parent conclusion is assumed, so the proof and empty dependency list are complete and non-circular.
